addresses.name: CPersistent::Save
addresses.comment: Slot 1 of CPersistent, and the whole of an object's braces: it writes `{`, calls slot 2 for the class's own keys, then indents and writes `}`. addresses.comment: What a unit type will cost this country in all - the whole build, not a day of it. Four arguments: the definition, the country, and somewhere to put an IC figure and a manpower one, either of which may be null to skip that half; both come back as fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>. addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildCost
addresses.comment: What this country pays for a building: the building's own cost (CBuilding +0x58) scaled by the discount its technology category earns, cost x (1000 - discount) / 1000. The slot 2 call on the category that guards it is the folded `mov al,1; ret` at 0xA92590, true for a real category and for the nocategory object alike, so the discount is always applied. That matters for a building whose category is nocategory - its index is 0, where every country's ability is 0, and an ability below 5.000 raises the cost: A building whose category is nocategory therefore costs about half as much again.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildCostIC
addresses.comment: What a unit type costs this country. base is the definition's BuildCostIC (+0xF8); the multiplier is 1000, plus CTechnologyStatus +0x24C for the type, plus the third argument times 10 (so 1% a point), less the discount the definition's technology category (+0x3C) earns - the same 0xE1AC0 buildings use. Then, where the fourth argument is set, times (1000 + the country's RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE modifier, 77) over 1000. The third argument is the caller's: the game works it out at 0x63D40 by adding up CTechnologyStatus +0x218 over the definition's own technology list (+0x44..+0x48). Only Lua calls this entry point; the game's own path is GetTotalBuildCost (0x63D40), which works the same cost out inline without the reserves step and multiplies it by GetBuildTime.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildTime
addresses.comment: How long a unit type takes this country to build. The definition's BuildTime (+0x100) times two factors over a million. The first is 1000, plus CTechnologyStatus +0x26C for the type, plus the second argument times 10, plus the country's UNIT_RECRUITMENT_TIME modifier (51), less the discount the definition's technology category earns (0xE1AC0, the same one the costs use); it is floored at 50. The second is 1000 plus one build speed modifier, chosen by the definition's kind flags in this order: is_rocket (+0x33) ROCKET_BUILD_SPEED, is_tank (+0x34) TANK_BUILD_SPEED, is_air (+0x2C) AIR_BUILD_SPEED, is_ship (+0x2E) NAVAL_BUILD_SPEED, else LAND_BUILD_SPEED.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall GetCategoryBuildDiscount(CCountry* country, int* out, CTechnologyCategory* category)
addresses.comment: The discount a technology category earns, in thousandths, which the build cost is scaled by as (1000 - this). Takes the country's ability in that category - its own level at +0x698, or the sharer's if a tag at +0x6A8 names one with a higher level, the same lookup GetAbility makes - floors it at 0 and measures it against 5.000: below that the result is negative and the cost goes up, at 100 per point; above it 50 per point with everything past 1.000 halved first. Then adds the country's INDUSTRIAL_EFFICIENCY modifier (74) and CTechnologyStatus +0x94, and caps the whole at 990, so at most 99% off. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CCountry::LoadOobFile
addresses.comment:
**Reads the order of battle named at `CCountry::oob_file`** and puts it in the country. It builds `<base>/units/<path>` - the base chosen by `[0x1685558 + 0x50]`, which has three values - and tries it with FileExists; then allocates a CParseContext (0x360 bytes) and a Tokenizer (0x114) over the file and calls **the country's own slot 3, `CPersistent::Load`**, with that context, before deleting it.

So **an order of battle is read as a piece of a country's save block**: Load pulls keys and hands each to `CCountry::LoadKey` (`0xCCDA0`), the same one a savegame goes through, and every keyword in the file is a SaveToken - `theatre` 1125, `armygroup` 1126, `corps` 1127, `division` 1128, `navy` 593, `air` 1088, `regiment` 594, `location` 544, `leader` 616, `military_construction` 637. **This is where the units are made.** The name is BiceLib's.

**Empties the string at the start of every record in a range**, walking `[first, last)` in steps of **0x20** and giving each string's buffer back where it had one - `if (capacity >= 0x10) free(data)`, then capacity 0xF, length 0, first byte 0. Both ends arrive in registers, first in eax and last in edi. `ret`.

It is a destructor loop the compiler wrote once and **1552 call sites share**: every record type of 0x20 bytes that begins with a string folds onto this one body, which is why its callers have nothing to do with each other. The stride is baked in, so it is only correct for that shape.

BiceLib meets it tearing a text object down: after ReleaseTextReplacements has destroyed the object each replacement points at, this empties the name each one carries, and the caller frees the block. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: free
addresses.comment: A thunk to the CRT's free. Every string destructor in the executable calls it the same way - `if (capacity > 15) free(pointer)` - which is what BiceLib copies to give back a string the game allocated for it.

addresses.name: _purecall
addresses.comment: The CRT stub a class's own vftable holds for a method it leaves pure virtual - COrder's slot 16, the order type id, among many. It calls the installed _purecall_handler if there is one and otherwise ends the process through _amsg_exit(_RT_PUREVIRT), the R6025 "pure virtual function call" message, so reaching it is fatal. Nothing reaches it in a working game: every concrete class fills the slot. Three Lua registrations resolve here - CCommand::IsValid, CDiplomaticAction::IsValid and CDiplomaticAction::GetAIAcceptance - because those methods are pure virtual in the class that declares them; the findings used to name this address after them (Shared_GetAIAcceptance_IsValid) and no longer do.

addresses.name: Return_1
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 1; ret` - the whole body, so the linker folded it and this one address fills a virtual table slot in several classes that have nothing to do with each other. It is slot 11 of CLandCombat, where it answers the combat kind 1, and that is written on CLandCombat's own slot rather than on the address.

addresses.name: Return_2
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 2; ret` - the whole body, so the linker folded it and this one address fills a virtual table slot in several classes that have nothing to do with each other. It is slot 11 of CNavalCombat, where it answers the combat kind 2, and that is written on CNavalCombat's own slot rather than on the address.

addresses.name: Define10
addresses.comment: A define, 10 - the floor of the float 10.5, taken at startup. Thousandths, so 0.010. Ten places read it and they do not agree on a purpose, so the name only says what it holds. CUnit's supply and fuel consumption (0x1BB560, 0x1BB7A0) add `CRegiment +0xCC x this` to a potency whose base is 1000, so each point of that field is 1% more consumption. Elsewhere it is a floor on a multiplier (0x1C30B6 clamps 1000 + x up to it before scaling max_strength), a threshold (0x1C638A) and an additive base (0x1CDA8C). addresses.name: Define50

CUnit's supply and fuel consumption multiply the army group leader's skill (CLeader +0x70) by it, scaled by how far that HQ's command reaches; the other three compare it against a unit's supply_received_percentage (+0xFC) and fuel_received_percentage (+0x100) to flag a unit that is short. 0x16886E8 is a separate global holding the same value from the same float. vftable_slots._about: Slot names BiceLib has established but that cannot be read off the slot's body - the linker folds identical bodies together, so the three unit predicates are one `mov al,1; ret` and one `xor al,al; ret` between them. Keyed by class, then slot. A record on a base class names that slot in every table below it, which is how CPersistent's six virtuals reach all 754 classes that derive from it; a name read off the slot's own body wins over one inherited this way.
